content:
Apple has officially reclaimed its position as the world's most valuable company. The company's stock price rose 17 points this week, surpassing Nvidia during Friday's intraday trading.

Apple's market capitalization is steadily approaching the $5 trillion mark, with its market value having touched the $4.9 trillion level. Previously, Nvidia had become the first company to break through the $5 trillion market capitalization threshold.

Apple's stock performance on Friday extended the company's recent momentum of repeatedly hitting new highs.

Apple had earlier unusually raised prices on Mac, iPad and other products due to the ongoing global memory shortage, causing a temporary dip in its stock price. However, after a full week of trading, the stock has fully recovered its losses and rebounded.

The company's next milestone will be breaking through the $5 trillion market capitalization.

Meanwhile, Apple is undergoing a CEO transition, with Tim Cook handing over the reins to John Ternus. The relevant announcement was officially made earlier this year, and August this year will be Cook's final month as Apple's CEO, after which he will remain on the board as executive chairman.
